free_tier.stated: Quoted, read 2026-10-22: 'New accounts can get $5 in free credit once they add and confirm an email address or make a first paid deposit, if Lium's abuse checks pass. It expires after 14 days.' The same page documents a one-call signup quoting: 'curl -fsS -X POST https://lium.io/api/auth/signup -d {}' returning 'signup_credit_granted': true. Lium's own llms-full.txt gives the grant condition in full: 'It is false when the platform has the credit off, and when this IP already signed up once.'

chaining: The credit is spendable only where a node is actually free, and the free nodes are all datacenter cards, so the USD 5 composes into 20.8 hours on an RTX 3090 or 1.3 to 2.5 hours on an H100 depending on tier; it does not compose into the cheap-tier hours the reference price suggests.

notes: CORRECTION TO BATCH 1, which recorded identity_cost 'anonymous'. The grant is not granted to an anonymous account: it requires a confirmed email address or a paid deposit, so the identity cost of the credit is at least email and is 'card' if the deposit route is used. Batch 1 also recorded 'USD 0.06 per GPU-hour, about 83 GPU-hours'. That arithmetic is right and the availability is zero: the RTX 3060 model shows available_gpus 0 today, and 15 nodes are rentable in total. The realistic figure is 20.8 hours at the cheapest rentable rate. What the credit does NOT cover is not established either way: the billing page charges pods, volumes and backups from the same balance, so in practice it covers all three. No first-party statement says what happens to an unused credit at 14 days beyond the expiry sentence. No third-party account of a credit being spent or clawed back was found in eight searches, so that question is open. One exact term batch 1 did not record: 'With only the $5 credit you can rent nodes below $20 per hour', which excludes 9 of the 14 nodes rentable today and leaves 5, of which 2 are the cheap RTX 3090s. qualifies-with-caveat via a04-decentralized. The one recorded is the better-evidenced.
